payload.name: SearchProfileBeforeWhichActivityAnswer
payload.description: When a question asks which activity helps a person achieve a benefit, and the first search returns memories for only one activity, run an additional profile/interest search for other hobbies and use those hobbies as query expansions before answering.
content: If a 'which activity helps [person] [benefit]' question yields initial results for only one activity type, first search the person's profile/interest memories (e.g., '[person] hobbies interests') before committing to an answer.

Use any hobbies found in those profile memories as additional semantic/BM25 query expansions, and stop once you have multiple distinct candidate activities or an explicit memory linking one activity to the benefit.
Do not apply this extra search when the question names a specific activity or when initial results already contain multiple distinct activity types.

solves: Questions like 'which activity helps X escape/stimulates imagination' can be answered wrongly when a literal paraphrase search retrieves only one activity (e.g., gaming) and misses the person's profile/interest memory naming another candidate activity. The Skill applies to future 'which activity provides [benefit]' questions where the answer is an unstated alternative present in profile memories. It must not apply when the question already names the activity or when the initial retrieval already surfaces multiple distinct candidate activities.
